definition_zh: 作者，作家；发起者，创始人；撰写，创作
definition_en: a person who writes a book or other work, the person who started a plan or idea, or to write something
core_image: 书页最上方印着一个人的名字，下面才是正文
scene: 新书发布会上，主持人请写这本书的人先讲两句。The author signed copies for two hours.
sceneCN: 这里 author 是「作者、作家」（第 1 个义项）；句意是作者签了两个小时的书。

derivatives.zh: 名词：作者身份；著作权
形容词：作者的
名词：合著者

senses.title: Writer of a work
senses.definition: a person who writes a book, article or other text
senses.definitionCN: 写书、写文章或其他文字作品的人
senses.example: The author signed copies for two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 作者签了两个小时的书。
senses.why: The Latin source auctor meant an originator, so the writer is seen as the person from whom the text comes.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源 auctor 意为「开创者」，所以作者被视为文本从之而来的那个人。

senses.title: Person who started something
senses.definition: the person who first thought of or started a plan, idea or change
senses.definitionCN: 最先想到或发起某个计划、想法、变革的人
senses.example: She is the author of the reform.
senses.exampleCN: 她是这场改革的发起者。
senses.why: The word keeps its older sense of originator: nothing needs to be written down for someone to be the author of a plan.
senses.whyCN: 这个词保留了「开创者」的旧义：要成为一项计划的发起者，并不需要真的写下什么。

senses.title: Write something
senses.definition: to write a book, report or other work yourself
senses.definitionCN: 亲自写出书、报告或其他作品
senses.example: He authored three reports on the case.
senses.exampleCN: 他就这个案子撰写了三份报告。
senses.why: The verb is modern and slightly formal; it stresses who produced the text rather than the act of writing itself.
senses.whyCN: 动词用法较新且偏正式，强调的是文本由谁产出，而不是书写这个动作本身。

intro.en: Author and authority grow from the same Latin word for an originator.
intro.cn: author 与 authority 出自同一个表示「开创者」的拉丁词。

items.en: augere meant 'to increase or make grow'.
items.cn: augere 意为「增加、使生长」。

items.en: auctor meant 'originator, promoter or seller'.
items.cn: auctor 意为「开创者、推动者、让与者」。

items.en: autor named the writer of a work.
items.cn: 古法语 autor 指作品的写作者。

items.en: English author covered both writer and founder.
items.cn: 中古英语 author 兼指写作者与创立者。

items.en: A verb use appeared, meaning to write a work.
items.cn: 现代英语又出现动词用法，意为撰写作品。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the auctor root; the near-meaning group gives words for writers and creators.
note.cn: 形近组共享 auctor 词根；近义组是表示写作者与创造者的词。

normalIntro.en: An author is where a text or a plan begins.
normalIntro.cn: author 就是文本或计划的起点。

normal.en: The root auctor means originator, which is why a plan can have an author.
normal.cn: 词根 auctor 意为开创者，所以一项计划也能有 author。

normal.en: The noun is common; the verb is formal and usually about reports or books.
normal.cn: 名词很常见；动词偏正式，多用于报告或书。

normal.en: Authority is not a person but the power an author figure holds.
normal.cn: authority 不是人，而是作者式人物握有的权力。

normal.en: Co-author adds co- for a shared writer.
normal.cn: co-author 加 co- 表示共同写作的人。

normal.en: Authorship names the fact of being the author.
normal.cn: authorship 指作者身份这件事。

abstract.cn: 想象扉页上书名上方印着一个名字。

abstract.cn: 想象一只手写完最后一行，把笔放下。

definition_zh: 权力，职权；当局，官方机构；权威，专家；权威性
definition_en: the power to give orders, an official body that has such power, a person whose knowledge is trusted, or the quality of being reliable
core_image: 一枚印章压在文件上，纸面立刻有了分量
scene: 小区要修路，居民先去找能拍板的那一方。The local authority approved the plan.

senses.title: Power to give orders
senses.definition: the right or power to give orders and make decisions
senses.definitionCN: 下命令、作决定的资格或力量
senses.example: The manager has the authority to hire staff.
senses.exampleCN: 这位经理有权雇用员工。
senses.why: The Latin source auctor meant an originator, and the derived noun named the weight an originator carries, so authority is power that comes from standing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源 auctor 意为开创者，派生名词指开创者身上的分量，所以 authority 是由地位带来的权力。

senses.title: Official body
senses.definition: an official organization or government body with power in an area
senses.definitionCN: 在某领域拥有权力的官方组织或政府机构
senses.example: The local authority approved the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 地方当局批准了这项计划。
senses.why: Power is transferred from a person to an institution, so the plural authorities often means the people who run a city or a service.
senses.whyCN: 权力从个人转到机构身上，所以复数 authorities 常指管理一座城市或某项公共事务的部门。

senses.title: Trusted expert
senses.definition: a person whose knowledge or judgment is respected and trusted
senses.definitionCN: 知识或判断受人尊重与信任的人
senses.example: She is an authority on ancient coins.
senses.exampleCN: 她是古钱币方面的权威。
senses.why: Here the weight is intellectual rather than official: the person is trusted because of knowledge, not because of an office.
senses.whyCN: 这里的分量是知识上的而非官职上的：此人受信任靠的是学问，而不是职位。

intro.en: Authority names the weight that an originator carries.
intro.cn: authority 指开创者身上所带的分量。

items.cn: auctor 意为「开创者、推动者」。

items.en: auctoritas meant 'influence, weight or command'.

items.en: autorite carried the sense of rightful power.

items.en: The plural became the normal word for official bodies.
items.cn: 复数形式成为指官方机构的常用说法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the auctor root; the near-meaning group gives words for power and expertise.

normalIntro.en: Authority is weight: official weight, institutional weight, or the weight of knowledge.
normalIntro.cn: authority 是一种分量：官职的分量、机构的分量，或知识的分量。

normal.en: The root is the same as in author: an originator carries weight.
normal.cn: 词根与 author 相同：开创者身上带着分量。

normal.en: The plural authorities usually means official bodies, not several powers.

normal.en: An authority on a subject is a trusted expert.
normal.cn: an authority on a subject 指某领域可信的专家。

normal.en: The adjective authoritative keeps the -ative ending.

normal.en: Do not confuse authority with author; one is weight, the other is a person.

sensesIntro.en: One word covers the right to command, the body that commands, and the expert who is trusted.

definition_zh: 自动的；无意识的，习惯性的；必然的
definition_en: working by itself without a person, done without thinking, or certain to happen as a result
core_image: 门在人走近时自己滑开，没有谁去推
scene: 手里拎着东西走到门口，门先一步让开。The doors are automatic, so you need not touch them.
sceneCN: 这里 automatic 是「自动的」（第 1 个义项：机器自己运作）；句意是这些门是自动的，不用手碰。

pos.zh: 形容词：自动的；无意识的；必然的

senses.title: Machine works alone
senses.definition: working by itself without a person operating it
senses.definitionCN: 不需要人操作就能自己运转的
senses.example: The doors are automatic, so you need not touch them.
senses.exampleCN: 这些门是自动的，不用手碰。
senses.why: Greek automatos described something acting of its own will, and machines took over that sense: the mechanism plays the role of the will.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 automatos 描述「按自己的意愿行动」，机器接过了这层意思：机械装置扮演了意愿的角色。

senses.title: Done without thinking
senses.definition: done as a habit or reflex, without conscious thought
senses.definitionCN: 作为习惯或本能做出，不经思考的
senses.example: Answering the phone is automatic for her.
senses.exampleCN: 接电话对她来说是不假思索的事。
senses.why: A person can also run on autopilot: the body acts by itself, so the machine word is applied to human habit.
senses.whyCN: 人也能靠「自动驾驶」运转：身体自己动起来，于是这个机器词被用到人的习惯上。

senses.title: Certain to follow
senses.definition: certain to happen as a natural result of something
senses.definitionCN: 作为某事的自然结果必然发生的
senses.example: A price cut means an automatic rise in sales.
senses.exampleCN: 降价必然带来销量上升。
senses.why: If a result follows a cause with no choice involved, it is automatic in the logical sense, like a machine that cannot do otherwise.
senses.whyCN: 如果结果毫无选择地跟着原因出现，它在逻辑意义上就是自动的，像一台不可能有别的动作的机器。

intro.en: Automatic first described things that move by their own will.
intro.cn: automatic 最初描述「按自己的意愿行动」的东西。

items.en: French automatique applied the idea to machinery.

items.en: English extended it to habits and inevitable results.
items.cn: 英语又把它扩展到习惯动作与必然结果。

normalIntro.en: Automatic moves the idea of self from a person to a machine, then back to a habit.
normalIntro.cn: automatic 把「自己」这个念头从人移到机器，再移回人的习惯。

normal.en: The prefix auto- means self, so automatic means acting by itself.
normal.cn: 前缀 auto- 意为「自己」，所以 automatic 就是自己动作。

normal.en: Automatic doors and automatic updates are the most common modern uses.
normal.cn: 自动门与自动更新是它最常见的现代用法。

normal.en: An automatic response is a reflex, not a decision.

normal.en: The adverb adds -ally: automatically.
normal.cn: 副词形式加 -ally，变成 automatically。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with automated, which describes a process converted to machines.
normal.cn: 不要与 automated 混淆，后者描述被改成机器运作的流程。

senses.title: By machine, unaided
senses.definition: by a machine or system working without a person's action
senses.definitionCN: 由机器或系统在人不出手的情况下完成
senses.example: The file saves automatically every minute.
senses.exampleCN: 文件每分钟自动保存。
senses.why: The adverb describes the manner of the action: no hand is involved, because the mechanism supplies the movement.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词描述动作的方式：没有手参与，因为动作由机械装置提供。

senses.title: Without thinking
senses.definition: as an unthinking habit or reflex
senses.definitionCN: 作为不经思考的习惯或本能
senses.example: She automatically assumes the worst.
senses.exampleCN: 她总是想当然地往最坏处想。
senses.why: The machine image moves to the mind: a habit runs on its own, so the person reaches the conclusion with no deliberate step.
senses.whyCN: 机器的意象转到心里：习惯自行运转，于是人没有经过刻意的步骤就得出这个结论。

senses.title: As a sure result
senses.definition: as a result that must follow
senses.definitionCN: 作为必定随之出现的结果
senses.example: Prices automatically rise when supply falls.
senses.exampleCN: 供给下降时，价格必然上涨。
senses.why: When one change forces another with no alternative, the adverb marks that inevitability rather than any machine.
senses.whyCN: 当一个变化迫使另一个变化、别无选择时，这个副词标记的是那种必然性，而不是任何机器。

senses.title: The season between summer and winter

senses.why: Autumn comes from Latin autumnus, the Roman name for the season of harvest and falling leaves, and English kept that place in the year.

senses.why: Harvest comes and leaves fall after the full summer, and a life that has passed its prime looks the same, so autumn can name its later stage.

definition_en: able to be obtained or used, free to see someone, or still open to be bought
core_image: 货架上还留着一件，手伸过去就能拿到
scene: 订票页面刷新了一下，原本灰掉的座位重新亮起。Two seats are still available.
sceneCN: 这里 available 是「可获得的、可用的」（第 1 个义项：还能拿到）；句意是还有两个座位可选。

pos.zh: 形容词：可获得的；有空的；有效的

derivatives.zh: 名词：可获得性；可得性
形容词：不可获得的；没空的

senses.title: Able to be had
senses.definition: able to be obtained, bought or used
senses.definitionCN: 能够被取得、买到或使用的
senses.example: Two seats are still available.
senses.exampleCN: 还有两个座位可选。
senses.why: The word is built on avail, 'to be of use or worth', so available describes something that is there and can be put to use.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在 avail「有用、有价值」之上，所以 available 描述的是东西就在那里、可以拿来用。

senses.title: Free to meet
senses.definition: not busy, and therefore free to meet or talk
senses.definitionCN: 不忙，因此可以见面或交谈
senses.example: The doctor is available after three.
senses.exampleCN: 医生三点以后有空。
senses.why: A person, like a thing, can be on hand and ready to be used; here the use is someone's time rather than an object.
senses.whyCN: 人像物品一样，可以在手边、随时可用；只是这里的「用」指的是对方的时间，而不是物件。

senses.title: Still open to buy
senses.definition: not yet sold or booked, and therefore still open to customers
senses.definitionCN: 尚未售出或订走，因此仍向顾客开放
senses.example: The ticket is available until Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 这张票在周五之前都能买。
senses.why: In ticketing the word narrows to stock that has not been taken, which is why it so often appears beside seats and rooms.
senses.whyCN: 在售票语境里，这个词收窄为「还没被拿走的名额」，所以常与座位、房间一起出现。

intro.en: Available grows from an old verb meaning to be of worth or use.
intro.cn: available 来自一个古老动词，意为「有价值、有用处」。

items.en: valoir meant 'to be worth'.

items.en: English avail kept the sense of being useful.

items.en: The adjective named what can be used or obtained.

normalIntro.cn: available 表示某物或某人在那里、可以用得上。

normal.en: The base is avail, to be of use, plus -able, able to.
normal.cn: 词基是 avail「有用」，加 -able「能够」。

normal.en: Available to names who may use it; available for names the purpose.
normal.cn: available to 引出可以使用的人，available for 引出用途。

normal.en: For people it means not busy, as in the doctor is available.
normal.cn: 用于人时表示不忙，例如医生有空。

normal.en: Readily available means easy to get, not merely existing.
normal.cn: readily available 表示容易得到，不只是存在。

normal.en: Unavailable adds un- and means the opposite.
normal.cn: 加 un- 构成 unavailable，意思相反。

abstract.cn: 想象货架上还剩下最后一件。

abstract.en: See an open door and a free chair in an office.

root: 源自中古英语 avail「有用、有价值」，更早来自古法语 availer 与拉丁语 valere「有力量、有价值」；加形容词词尾 -able 后表示「可以被取得或使用」，再由物及人，引申为「有空」。

sensesIntro.en: A product, a person's time and an unsold ticket can all be available.
sensesIntro.cn: 一件商品、一个人的时间、一张没卖出的票，都可以是 available。

definition_zh: 平均数；平均的；普通的；平均为
definition_en: the middle amount or level, or to amount to such a level
core_image: 一排高低不齐的柱子被一条水平线穿过
scene: 老师在讲台上翻开成绩册。The average score of the class rose this term.
sceneCN: 这里 average 是「平均数」（第 1 个义项：把总数按份数均分得到的值）；句意是这个班的平均分本学期提高了。

derivatives.zh: 由 average 加 -ly 构成，义为「平均地；普通地」
由 average 与 sized 复合而成，义为「中等大小的」

senses.title: The middle amount
senses.definition: the result of adding several amounts and dividing by their number
senses.definitionCN: 把若干数量相加后除以个数所得的结果
senses.example: The average of three, five and seven is five.
senses.exampleCN: 三、五、七的平均数是五。
senses.why: Average comes from French avarie, damage to goods at sea, because a shared loss was divided among merchants; the arithmetic sense grew from dividing a total fairly.
senses.whyCN: average 来自法语 avarie「海损」，因为共同损失要由商人分摊；算术上的「平均」正是从这种平摊长出来的。

senses.title: Typical or ordinary
senses.definition: ordinary and not special or unusual
senses.definitionCN: 普通而并无特别之处的
senses.example: She is an average student who works hard.
senses.exampleCN: 她是个努力用功的普通学生。
senses.why: If an average is the middle of a range, then a person or thing near that middle is ordinary, neither very good nor very bad.
senses.whyCN: 既然平均数是区间的中点，那么处在中点附近的人或物就是普通的，不算特别好也不算特别差。

senses.title: To amount to as a mean
senses.definition: to reach an average of a particular amount over time
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间里达到某个平均数值
senses.example: Sales averaged two hundred units a month.
senses.exampleCN: 每月销量平均为两百件。
senses.why: The noun meaning the middle value turned into a verb meaning to produce that middle value over time.
senses.whyCN: 表示中间值的名词转成动词，就表示在一段时间里得出那个平均值。

intro.cn: average 最初是一个讲海上共同损失的说法。

items.en: The word settled on the sense of a middle value.
items.cn: 这个词最后固定为「平均值」之义。

normalIntro.cn: average 把高低不齐的数量摊成一条水平线，再把这个水平称作普通。

normal.en: Average has three syllables, with the stress on the first.

normal.en: Use on average to speak about a general level.

normal.en: Above average and below average mark the two sides.

normal.en: Do not confuse average with avarice, which means greed.

sensesIntro.en: A fair share, a middle value and an ordinary level are one idea seen from three sides.

core_image: 脚在最后一刻抬起来，跨过地上的水洼
scene: 路面刚下过雨，行人绕开积水。She stepped aside to avoid the puddle.

senses.title: Stay away from
senses.definition: to keep away from a person, place or thing
senses.definitionCN: 远离某人、某地或某物
senses.example: She stepped aside to avoid the puddle.
senses.exampleCN: 她侧身让开，避开了那摊水。
senses.why: Avoid comes from Old French esvuidier, to empty out, from vuide, empty; to avoid a place was to leave it empty and then to keep clear of it.
senses.whyCN: avoid 来自古法语 esvuidier「清空」，源于 vuide「空的」；把某地腾空，就是离开它，再引申为躲开它。

senses.title: Prevent from happening
senses.definition: to stop something bad from happening
senses.definitionCN: 阻止不好的事情发生
senses.example: Careful driving can avoid many accidents.
senses.exampleCN: 谨慎驾驶可以避免许多事故。
senses.why: If you keep clear of a risk, the bad event never occurs, so the same verb came to mean preventing it.
senses.whyCN: 躲开风险，坏事就不会发生，于是同一个动词又表示「防止」。

senses.title: Not do something

senses.definitionCN: 有意不去做某事
senses.example: He avoided answering the question.

senses.why: Leaving a thing empty extends to leaving an action undone, which is why avoid often takes an -ing form.

normalIntro.en: Avoid is about leaving a space empty, and so keeping clear of trouble.

abstract.en: See a hand pulling back from a hot pan.

examples.en: She stepped aside to avoid the puddle.

examples.cn: 谨慎驾驶可以避免许多事故。

sensesIntro.en: Leaving a place, a risk or an action all begin with making space.

a time left empty of work

definition_en: not asleep, or to stop sleeping
core_image: 天刚亮，眼睛突然睁开
scene: 窗帘缝里透进第一道晨光。The baby was awake before dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 awake 是「醒着的」（第 1 个义项：没有睡着）；句意是婴儿在天亮前就醒了。

derivatives.zh: 由 awake 加 -en 构成，义为「唤醒；使觉醒」
由 awaken 加 -ing 构成，义为「觉醒」
基础词，义为「醒来」，与 awake 同源

senses.title: Not asleep
senses.definition: not sleeping
senses.definitionCN: 没有睡着的
senses.example: The baby was awake before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿在天亮前就醒了。
senses.why: Awake is the old adjective from the verb wacan, to wake, and it describes the state rather than the act.
senses.whyCN: awake 是古动词 wacan「醒来」变来的形容词，描述的是状态而不是动作。

senses.title: Stop sleeping
senses.definition: to stop sleeping, or to make someone stop sleeping
senses.definitionCN: 停止睡眠，或使某人停止睡眠
senses.example: She awoke to the sound of rain.
senses.exampleCN: 她在雨声中醒来。
senses.why: The same word works as a verb because waking is both what happens to you and what someone does to you.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也能作动词，因为醒来既可以是自己发生的，也可以是别人把你弄醒。

senses.title: Become aware of
senses.definition: to become conscious of something
senses.definitionCN: 开始意识到某事
senses.example: He awoke to the danger of the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 他意识到了这个计划的危险。
senses.why: Waking from sleep is a natural image for the mind becoming alert, so awake to came to mean realizing.
senses.whyCN: 从睡眠中醒来很适合比喻头脑变得警觉，所以 awake to 表示「意识到」。

intro.en: Awake goes back to a Germanic word for being watchful.
intro.cn: awake 可上溯到日耳曼语中表示「警醒」的词。

items.en: wacan meant 'to wake'.
items.cn: wacan 意为「醒来」。

items.en: wacian meant 'to be awake'.
items.cn: wacian 意为「醒着」。

items.en: awake served as both adjective and verb.
items.cn: awake 兼作形容词与动词。

items.en: awaken grew beside awake.
items.cn: awaken 与 awake 并行使用。

items.en: The adjective use is now the most common.
items.cn: 如今形容词用法最常见。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the a- opening; the near-meaning group gives states and acts of waking.
note.cn: 形近组都以 a- 开头；近义组是表示清醒状态与醒来动作的词。

normalIntro.en: Awake describes the state, while awaken usually describes the act of waking someone.
normalIntro.cn: awake 描述状态，awaken 多描述把人唤醒的动作。

normal.en: Awake is usually an adjective after be or stay.
normal.cn: awake 多作形容词，放在 be 或 stay 之后。

normal.en: The past tense is awoke and the participle awoken.
normal.cn: 过去式是 awoke，过去分词是 awoken。

normal.en: Wide awake means fully awake.
normal.cn: wide awake 意为完全清醒。

normal.en: Awake to something means realizing it.
normal.cn: awake to 某事意为意识到它。

normal.en: Do not put awake before a noun in everyday speech.
normal.cn: 日常口语中不把 awake 放在名词前。

abstract.en: See eyes opening at the first grey light.
abstract.cn: 想象天刚泛灰时眼睛睁开。

abstract.en: See a hand switching off an alarm.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手关掉闹钟。

abstract.en: See a sleeper sitting up suddenly.
abstract.cn: 想象睡着的人突然坐起。

examples.en: The baby was awake before dawn.
examples.cn: 婴儿在天亮前就醒了。

examples.en: She awoke to the sound of rain.
examples.cn: 她在雨声中醒来。

examples.en: He awoke to the danger of the plan.
examples.cn: 他意识到了这个计划的危险。

dict_mnemonic.text: a- 加 wake（醒）：从睡梦里睁开眼，是醒来；脑子从糊涂里睁开眼，是意识到。

root: 源自古英语 wacan「醒来」与 wacian「醒着」，属日耳曼语系；中古英语起兼作形容词与动词，awaken 为后起形式。

sensesIntro.en: Being awake, waking up and waking to a fact are three degrees of the same alertness.
sensesIntro.cn: 醒着、醒来与醒悟，是同一种警觉的三个程度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: eyes opening at first light.
core.cn: 核心意象：第一道晨光里眼睛睁开。

intro.en: The wake root, 'to be alert', also gives wake, awaken and waking.
intro.cn: 词根 wake 意为「警醒」，也构成 wake、awaken 与 waking。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base here; the family is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，这一族词来自日耳曼语。

definition_en: a prize given for achievement, or to give such a prize officially
core_image: 一只奖杯被递到伸出的双手上
scene: 典礼上掌声响起。The judge awarded her the first prize.
sceneCN: 这里 award 是「授予」（第 2 个义项：正式把奖项或款项给某人）；句意是评委把一等奖授予了她。

derivatives.zh: 由 award 加 -ee 构成，义为「获奖者」
由 award 与 winning 复合而成，义为「获奖的；屡获殊荣的」

senses.title: A prize
senses.definition: something given to someone for an achievement
senses.definitionCN: 因成就而发给某人的东西
senses.example: She received an award for her research.
senses.exampleCN: 她因研究成果获得了一个奖项。
senses.why: Award comes from Old French eswarder, to judge, so a prize is what a judge decides to give.
senses.whyCN: award 来自古法语 eswarder「评判」，所以奖项就是评判者决定给出的东西。

senses.title: Give officially
senses.definition: to give money or a prize officially
senses.definitionCN: 正式发给钱款或奖项
senses.example: The judge awarded her the first prize.
senses.exampleCN: 评委把一等奖授予了她。
senses.why: The noun for a decided gift turned into the verb for the deciding and giving.
senses.whyCN: 表示判定给予之物的名词，转成了表示判定并给予的动词。

senses.title: Decide legally
senses.definition: to decide that someone should receive money in a court
senses.definitionCN: 在法庭上裁定某人应得钱款
senses.example: The court awarded damages to the family.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭判给这家人损害赔偿金。
senses.why: A judge's decision is the oldest sense, and the courtroom is where the giving is most formal.
senses.whyCN: 评判者的裁定是最古老的义项，而法庭正是这种给予最正式的场合。

intro.en: Award is a word about judging before it is a word about prizes.
intro.cn: award 先是关于评判的词，然后才关于奖品。

items.en: warder meant 'to guard or watch'.
items.cn: warder 意为「看守、注视」。

items.en: eswarder meant 'to judge'.
items.cn: eswarder 意为「评判」。

items.en: awarder meant 'to decide'.
items.cn: awarder 意为「裁定」。

items.en: award meant a decision of a judge.
items.cn: award 意为法官的裁定。

items.en: The prize sense became the most common.
items.cn: 奖项义成为最常用的义项。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the aw opening; the near-meaning group gives prizes and grants.
note.cn: 形近组都以 aw 开头；近义组是表示奖品与授予的词。

normalIntro.en: An award is what a judge gives, while a reward is what you earn for service.
normalIntro.cn: award 是评判者给出的，reward 是因服务而得到的回报。

normal.en: The stress is on the second syllable: a-WARD.
normal.cn: 重音在第二音节。

normal.en: Use award for prizes and official payments.
normal.cn: award 用于奖项与正式款项。

normal.en: A reward is usually money for help or effort.
normal.cn: reward 通常是因帮助或努力得到的钱。

normal.en: The noun and the verb have the same form.
normal.cn: 名词与动词同形。

normal.en: An award-winning film is one that has won prizes.
normal.cn: award-winning 指获奖的。

abstract.en: See a trophy passed into two open hands.
abstract.cn: 想象一只奖杯被递到张开的双手上。

abstract.en: See a judge striking a small hammer.
abstract.cn: 想象法官敲下小锤。

abstract.en: See a name read out and a row of heads turning.
abstract.cn: 想象有人念出一个名字，一排脑袋转过去。

examples.en: She received an award for her research.
examples.cn: 她因研究成果获得了一个奖项。

examples.en: The judge awarded her the first prize.
examples.cn: 评委把一等奖授予了她。

examples.en: The court awarded damages to the family.
examples.cn: 法庭判给这家人损害赔偿金。

dict_mnemonic.text: a- 加 ward（看）：评判者看准了谁做得好，就把奖递过去，这就是授予。

root: 源自古法语 eswarder「评判」，与 warder「看守、注视」同源，经盎格鲁-诺曼语 awarder「裁定」进入英语；由法官裁定引申为授予奖项。

sensesIntro.en: A prize, an official gift and a legal ruling are all one judged decision.
sensesIntro.cn: 奖品、正式给予与法律裁定，都是同一个「经评判而给出」的决定。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cup handed into waiting hands.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只奖杯被递到等待的双手上。

intro.en: The ward root, 'to watch', also gives ward, guard and reward.
intro.cn: 词根 ward 意为「看守」，也构成 ward、guard 与 reward。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base here; the family comes from Germanic watch words through French.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，这一族词经法语来自日耳曼语表示「看守」的词。

items.meaning: a guard or a protected area
one who looks after a household

definition_zh: 意识到的；知道的；察觉到的
definition_en: knowing that something exists or is happening
core_image: 一个人忽然停下，侧耳听见远处的警笛
scene: 街角的行人同时抬起头。Everyone was aware of the siren behind them.
sceneCN: 这里 aware 是「意识到的」（第 1 个义项：知道某事存在或正在发生）；句意是每个人都察觉到了身后的警笛声。

pos.zh: 形容词：意识到的；知道的；察觉到的

derivatives.zh: 由 aware 加 -ness 构成，义为「意识；认识」
由 aware 加 un- 构成，义为「未察觉的」
由 self 与 aware 复合而成，义为「有自我意识的」

senses.title: Knowing something exists
senses.definition: knowing that something exists or is happening
senses.definitionCN: 知道某事存在或正在发生
senses.example: Everyone was aware of the siren behind them.
senses.exampleCN: 每个人都察觉到了身后的警笛声。
senses.why: Aware is an old adjective from ware, watchful; to be aware is to have your attention on something.
senses.whyCN: aware 是古形容词 ware「警觉的」的变体；aware 就是注意力落在某物上。

senses.title: Informed about a fact
senses.definition: having knowledge of a fact or situation
senses.definitionCN: 掌握某个事实或情况
senses.example: Are you aware that the office closes early today?
senses.exampleCN: 你知道办公室今天提前关门吗？
senses.why: Watchfulness grows into knowledge, so aware also means having information, especially information others may not have.
senses.whyCN: 警觉会发展成知识，所以 aware 也指掌握信息，尤其是别人未必知道的信息。

intro.en: Aware began as a word for being watchful.
intro.cn: aware 最初表示「警觉的」。

items.en: wær meant 'cautious or watchful'.
items.cn: wær 意为「谨慎、警觉」。

items.en: gewær meant 'aware'.
items.cn: gewær 意为「觉察到的」。

items.en: aware kept the sense of being watchful.
items.cn: aware 保留了警觉之义。

items.en: aware shifted toward knowing.
items.cn: aware 转向「知道」。

items.en: Aware of is now the usual pattern.
items.cn: 如今常用 aware of 的结构。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the a- opening; the near-meaning group gives kinds of knowing.
note.cn: 形近组都以 a- 开头；近义组是表示知道与留心的词。

normalIntro.en: Aware is watchfulness turned into knowledge.
normalIntro.cn: aware 是警觉变成了知识。

normal.en: Aware of is the usual pattern, and aware that also works.
normal.cn: 常用 aware of，也可接 aware that。

normal.en: The noun is awareness, not aware.
normal.cn: 名词是 awareness。

normal.en: Unaware means not knowing.
normal.cn: unaware 意为不知道的。

normal.en: Aware is not used before a noun in most speech.
normal.cn: 多数口语中 aware 不放在名词前。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: a-WARE.
normal.cn: 重音在第二音节。

abstract.en: See a walker stopping and turning an ear.
abstract.cn: 想象行人停下脚步侧耳倾听。

abstract.en: See a light switching on in a dark room.
abstract.cn: 想象暗房里一盏灯亮起。

abstract.en: See a hand raised to warn the person ahead.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手抬起提醒前面的人。

examples.en: Everyone was aware of the siren behind them.
examples.cn: 每个人都察觉到了身后的警笛声。

examples.en: Are you aware that the office closes early today?
examples.cn: 你知道办公室今天提前关门吗？

examples.en: She became aware of soft footsteps behind her.
examples.cn: 她察觉到身后有轻轻的脚步声。

dict_mnemonic.text: a- 加 ware（警觉）：眼睛和耳朵先醒过来，心里也就知道了。

root: 源自古英语 wær「谨慎、警觉」及其复合形式 gewær「觉察到的」，属日耳曼语系；由「警觉」引申为「知道、意识到」。

sensesIntro.en: Watchfulness and knowledge are two ends of the same attention.
sensesIntro.cn: 警觉与知识，是同一种注意力的两端。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an ear turning toward a distant sound.
core.cn: 核心意象：耳朵转向远处的声音。

intro.en: The ware root, 'watchful', also gives beware, wary and awareness.

definition_en: the state of knowing that something exists or is important
core_image: 一束灯光照亮原本黑暗的角落
scene: 社区公告栏前围了一圈人。The campaign raised awareness of water waste.
sceneCN: 这里 awareness 是「意识」（第 1 个义项：知道某事存在或重要）；句意是这场活动提高了人们对水资源浪费的意识。

derivatives.zh: 基础形容词，义为「意识到的」，awareness 由其加 -ness 构成

由 unaware 加 -ness 构成，义为「未察觉」

senses.title: The state of knowing
senses.definition: the state of knowing that something exists
senses.definitionCN: 知道某事存在的状态
senses.example: The campaign raised awareness of water waste.
senses.exampleCN: 这场活动提高了人们对水资源浪费的意识。
senses.why: Awareness is aware plus -ness, and the suffix turns a passing state of attention into a lasting condition of mind.
senses.whyCN: awareness 是 aware 加 -ness，后缀把一时的注意变成一种持续的心智状态。

senses.title: Public understanding
senses.definition: the extent to which people know and care about an issue
senses.definitionCN: 人们对某个议题了解与关心的程度
senses.example: Public awareness of the disease has grown.
senses.exampleCN: 公众对这种疾病的认识提高了。
senses.why: When many people hold the same knowledge, awareness becomes a social measure rather than a private feeling.
senses.whyCN: 当许多人共享同一种认识时，awareness 就从私人感受变成了社会性的衡量指标。

intro.en: Awareness is the noun built on the old word for watchfulness.

items.en: awareness meant the state of being aware.

items.en: It also names public attention to issues.

entries.definition: the state of being awake and aware

examples.en: Public awareness of the disease has grown.
examples.cn: 公众对这种疾病的认识提高了。

examples.en: She spoke with great awareness of the risks.
examples.cn: 她讲话时对这些风险有很清楚的认识。

dict_mnemonic.text: aware（警觉的）加 -ness（状态）：警觉停在心里成了常态，就是意识。

root: 由 aware 加名词后缀 -ness 构成；aware 源自古英语 wær「警觉」，属日耳曼语系；由「警觉的状态」引申为「意识、认识」。

sensesIntro.en: A private state of knowing and a public level of attention are the same noun at two scales.
sensesIntro.cn: 私人的知道与公共的关注度，是同一个名词的两种尺度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a beam of light reaching a dark corner.
core.cn: 核心意象：一束光照到黑暗的角落。

intro.en: The -ness suffix turns adjectives into state nouns, as in awareness and kindness.
intro.cn: 后缀 -ness 把形容词变成状态名词，如 awareness 与 kindness。

latinIntro.en: The base is Germanic, while the suffix is native English.
latinIntro.cn: 词基来自日耳曼语，后缀是英语本族成分。

definition_en: at a distance from a place or person, or into another place
core_image: 一只小船离开岸边，越划越远
scene: 傍晚的湖面很静。The boat drifted away from the shore.
sceneCN: 这里 away 是「离开」（第 1 个义项：从某处向远处移动）；句意是小船从岸边漂远了。

derivatives.zh: 由 far 与 away 复合而成，义为「遥远的」
由 run 与 away 复合而成，义为「逃跑的；失控的」

senses.title: To a distance
senses.definition: from a place or person toward another place
senses.definitionCN: 从某地或某人处向另一处
senses.example: The boat drifted away from the shore.
senses.exampleCN: 小船从岸边漂远了。
senses.why: Away is the old phrase on weg, on the way, so it began as motion along a road and kept the idea of leaving a point.
senses.whyCN: away 原是短语 on weg「在路上」，所以它起初指沿路移动，保留了「离开某一点」的意思。

senses.title: At a distance
senses.definition: at a distance from a particular place
senses.definitionCN: 距离某个地方有一定距离
senses.example: Her house is two miles away.
senses.exampleCN: 她家在两英里外。
senses.why: Once a person has left, the same word describes the resulting distance rather than the movement.
senses.whyCN: 人离开之后，同一个词就描述留下的距离，而不再描述移动。

senses.title: Disappearing or used up
senses.definition: gradually disappearing or being completely used
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐消失或被完全用掉
senses.example: The sound faded away.
senses.exampleCN: 声音渐渐消失了。
senses.why: Moving away can also describe a thing leaving existence, so away marks fading, ending and using up.
senses.whyCN: 移开也可以描述事物离开存在，所以 away 也标记消散、结束与用尽。

intro.en: Away began as a phrase meaning on the way.
intro.cn: away 原是一个意为「在路上」的短语。

items.en: on weg meant 'on the way'.
items.cn: on weg 意为「在路上」。

items.en: awei meant 'from this place'.
items.cn: awei 意为「离开此处」。

items.en: away covered distance as well as motion.
items.cn: away 兼指距离与移动。

items.en: It joined many verbs as a particle.
items.cn: 它作为小品词与许多动词结合。

items.en: Away now also marks fading and using up.
items.cn: 如今也标记消散与用尽。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the a- opening; the near-meaning group gives words of separation.
note.cn: 形近组都以 a- 开头；近义组是表示分离与距离的词。

normalIntro.en: Away is the picture of someone already on the road.
normalIntro.cn: away 画的是一个人已经上路走远的样子。

normal.en: Away follows verbs: go away, run away, put away.
normal.cn: away 跟在动词后，如走开、跑开、收起来。

normal.en: Far away puts the distance before the word.
normal.cn: far away 把距离放在前面。

normal.en: Right away means immediately.
normal.cn: right away 意为立刻。

normal.en: Away from home shows the starting point.
normal.cn: away from home 标出起点。

normal.en: The stress falls on the second syllable: a-WAY.
normal.cn: 重音在第二音节。

abstract.cn: 想象小船朝远岸越缩越小。

abstract.en: See footsteps fading down a corridor.
abstract.cn: 想象脚步声在走廊里渐渐远去。

abstract.en: See a hand putting a book back on a shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把书放回书架。

examples.cn: 小船从岸边漂远了。

examples.en: The sound faded away.
examples.cn: 声音渐渐消失了。

dict_mnemonic.text: a- 加 way（路）：人一上路就走远了，away 就是离开、在远处。

root: 源自古英语短语 on weg「在路上」，中古英语合为 awei，后写作 away；由「上路离开」引申为「在远处」与「消失、用尽」。

sensesIntro.en: Leaving, being far and fading out are three stages of the same departure.
sensesIntro.cn: 离开、在远处与消散，是同一次离去的三个阶段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boat moving from the shore into open water.
core.cn: 核心意象：小船离岸驶向开阔水面。

intro.en: The way root, 'road', also gives always and gateway.
intro.cn: 词根 way 意为「路」，也构成 always 与 gateway。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base here; away grew from an English phrase.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，away 从英语短语长成。

definition_en: very bad or unpleasant, or causing fear
core_image: 天空压下一片黑云，雷声在头顶炸开
scene: 山顶的风突然停了。An awful silence followed the thunder.
sceneCN: 这里 awful 是「可怕的」（第 1 个义项：令人恐惧或震撼的）；句意是雷声过后是一片可怕的寂静。

pos.zh: 形容词：可怕的；糟糕的；非常的

derivatives.zh: 由 awful 加 -ly 构成，义为「非常；糟糕地」
由 awful 加 -ness 构成，义为「糟糕；可怕」
基础词，义为「敬畏」，awful 由其加 -ful 构成

senses.title: Causing fear
senses.definition: very bad and frightening
senses.definitionCN: 非常糟糕且令人害怕的
senses.example: An awful silence followed the thunder.
senses.exampleCN: 雷声过后是一片可怕的寂静。
senses.why: Awful first meant 'full of awe', and awe was a mixture of fear and wonder, so the word began with terror rather than mere badness.
senses.whyCN: awful 最初意为「充满敬畏的」，而敬畏混杂着恐惧与惊叹，所以这个词起初指恐怖，而不只是「差」。

senses.title: Very bad
senses.definition: extremely unpleasant or of poor quality
senses.definitionCN: 令人很不愉快或质量很差的
senses.example: The weather was awful all week.
senses.exampleCN: 整个星期天气都很糟糕。
senses.why: As awe weakened in everyday speech, awful slid from terror to ordinary dislike, which is the sense most people use today.
senses.whyCN: 随着 awe 在日常口语中减弱，awful 从恐怖滑向普通的厌恶，这就是今天最常用的义项。

senses.title: Very great in amount
senses.definition: used to emphasize a large amount
senses.definitionCN: 用于强调数量很大
senses.example: It took an awful lot of work.
senses.exampleCN: 这花了非常多功夫。
senses.why: Something frightening is also overwhelming, so awful became an intensifier for size and degree.
senses.whyCN: 令人害怕的东西也让人招架不住，于是 awful 变成强调数量与程度的词。

intro.en: Awful is a word that fell from awe to mere dislike.
intro.cn: awful 是一个从敬畏跌落到单纯厌恶的词。

items.en: ege meant 'fear'.
items.cn: ege 意为「恐惧」。

items.en: awe meant fear mixed with wonder.
items.cn: awe 意为恐惧混杂惊叹。

items.en: aweful meant 'full of awe'.
items.cn: aweful 意为「充满敬畏的」。

items.en: awful meant 'frightful'.
items.cn: awful 意为「可怕的」。

items.en: It weakened to 'very bad'.
items.cn: 后来弱化为「很糟的」。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the awe base; the near-meaning group gives degrees of badness.
note.cn: 形近组都含 awe 词基；近义组是表示糟糕程度的词。

entries.definition: very, or in a bad way

normalIntro.en: Awful still carries the shadow of awe, even when it only means bad.
normalIntro.cn: 即使只表示「糟」，awful 仍带着敬畏的影子。

normal.en: Awful is stronger than bad but weaker than terrifying.
normal.cn: awful 比 bad 强，但比 terrifying 弱。

normal.en: An awful lot means a very large amount.
normal.cn: an awful lot 意为非常多。

normal.en: The adverb is awfully, not awful.
normal.cn: 副词是 awfully。

normal.en: The spelling keeps the w from awe.

abstract.en: See a crowd frozen by one loud crack.
abstract.cn: 想象一声巨响让整个人群僵住。

dict_mnemonic.text: awe（敬畏）加 -ful（充满）：满心敬畏，先是怕，后来变成嫌它糟。

root: 由 awe「敬畏」加 -ful「充满」构成，awe 源自古英语 ege「恐惧」并受古诺斯语 agi 影响；由「令人敬畏的」弱化为「可怕的、糟糕的」。

sensesIntro.en: Fear, dislike and sheer size are the three stops on the road from awe to awful.
sensesIntro.cn: 恐惧、厌恶与量太大，是 awful 从敬畏一路走来的三站。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a black cloud pressing down before thunder.
core.cn: 核心意象：雷声前压下来的黑云。

intro.en: The -ful suffix means 'full of', as in awful and hopeful.
intro.cn: 后缀 -ful 意为「充满」，如 awful 与 hopeful。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base here; the family is Germanic.

definition_en: causing embarrassment, or moving in a clumsy way
core_image: 两只手都不知该往哪儿放，站在门口进退不得
scene: 礼堂里忽然安静下来。He made an awkward joke at the wrong moment.
sceneCN: 这里 awkward 是「尴尬的」（第 1 个义项：令人不自在、难为情的）；句意是他在不合适的时机讲了个尴尬的笑话。

pos.zh: 形容词：尴尬的；笨拙的；难对付的

derivatives.zh: 由 awkward 加 -ly 构成，义为「尴尬地；笨拙地」
由 awkward 加 -ness 构成，义为「尴尬；笨拙」

senses.title: Causing embarrassment
senses.definition: causing embarrassment or making people uncomfortable
senses.definitionCN: 令人难为情或让人不自在的
senses.example: He made an awkward joke at the wrong moment.
senses.exampleCN: 他在不合适的时机讲了个尴尬的笑话。
senses.why: Awkward comes from Old Norse afugr, turned the wrong way, so the core image is something facing backwards and out of place.
senses.whyCN: awkward 来自古诺斯语 afugr「方向转反了」，核心意象是东西朝反了、位置不对。

senses.title: Clumsy in movement
senses.definition: moving or behaving in a clumsy way
senses.definitionCN: 动作或举止笨拙的
senses.example: The puppy was awkward on the smooth floor.
senses.exampleCN: 小狗在光滑的地板上走得很笨拙。
senses.why: A body facing the wrong way moves badly, so the same word names physical clumsiness.
senses.whyCN: 身体朝向不对就动得别扭，于是同一个词也指身体上的笨拙。

senses.title: Hard to deal with
senses.definition: difficult to use, handle or deal with
senses.definitionCN: 难以使用、处理或应付的
senses.example: The box was awkward to carry up the stairs.
senses.exampleCN: 这个箱子很难搬上楼。
senses.why: Anything that does not fit the situation is hard to handle, which extends the word from people to objects and timing.
senses.whyCN: 任何与情境不合的东西都难对付，这就把词从人扩展到物品与时机。

intro.en: Awkward is a word about facing the wrong way.
intro.cn: awkward 说的是方向转反了。

items.en: afugr meant 'turned the wrong way'.
items.cn: afugr 意为「方向转反的」。

items.en: afugligr meant 'unfavourable'.
items.cn: afugligr 意为「不顺的」。

items.en: aukeward meant 'backhanded'.
items.cn: aukeward 意为「反手的」。

items.en: awkward meant 'clumsy'.
items.cn: awkward 意为「笨拙的」。

items.en: It also means socially embarrassing.
items.cn: 如今也指社交上的尴尬。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the aw opening; the near-meaning group gives clumsiness and unease.
note.cn: 形近组都以 aw 开头；近义组是表示笨拙与不自在的词。

normalIntro.en: Awkward is the feeling of standing at the wrong angle to everything.
normalIntro.cn: awkward 是与一切都对不上角度的感觉。

normal.en: Awkward describes both people and situations.
normal.cn: awkward 既能形容人，也能形容处境。

normal.en: An awkward silence is a silence nobody can fill.
normal.cn: an awkward silence 是没人接得上的沉默。

normal.en: The adverb is awkwardly.
normal.cn: 副词是 awkwardly。

normal.en: The w in the middle is pronounced.
normal.cn: 中间的 w 要发音。

normal.cn: 重音在第一音节。

abstract.cn: 想象一把椅子背对着桌子。

root: 来自古诺斯语 afugr「方向转反的」，其派生 afugligr「不顺的」经中古英语 aukeward「反手的」进入英语；由「方向不对」引申为笨拙与尴尬。

sensesIntro.en: Wrong direction, clumsy body and difficult situation are the same misfit seen three ways.
sensesIntro.cn: 方向不对、动作笨拙与处境难办，是同一个「不合位」的三种看法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands hovering with nowhere to rest.

intro.en: The -ward suffix marks direction, as in awkward, backward and forward.

definition_en: a very young child, or a small version of something
core_image: 一只小拳头从襁褓里伸出来
scene: 摇篮边围着一家人。The baby slept through the loud music.
sceneCN: 这里 baby 是「婴儿」（第 1 个义项：很小的孩子）；句意是婴儿在吵闹的音乐声中一直睡着。

derivatives.zh: 由 baby 加 -ish 构成，义为「幼稚的」
由 baby 与 sit 复合而成，义为「照看孩子」
由 babysit 加 -er 构成，义为「保姆」

senses.title: A very young child
senses.definition: a very young child who cannot yet walk or talk
senses.definitionCN: 还不能走路或说话的幼小孩子
senses.example: The baby slept through the loud music.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿在吵闹的音乐声中一直睡着。
senses.why: Baby is a diminutive form of babe, which first meant a small child, so the word carries a built-in sense of smallness.
senses.whyCN: baby 是 babe 的指小形式，babe 原指小孩子，所以这个词自带「小」的意思。

senses.title: A small version
senses.definition: a small or young version of something
senses.definitionCN: 某物的小型或幼小版本
senses.example: She planted baby carrots in the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 她在园子里种了小胡萝卜。
senses.why: Because a baby is small, the word became a friendly label for small kinds of things, from vegetables to machines.
senses.whyCN: 因为婴儿很小，这个词就成了各种小东西的亲切标签，从蔬菜到机器都能用。

senses.title: A dear person
senses.definition: a word used for someone you love
senses.definitionCN: 对心爱之人的称呼
senses.example: Come here, baby, and sit with me.
senses.exampleCN: 过来，宝贝，陪我坐一会儿。
senses.why: Calling a loved one a baby borrows the tenderness of caring for an infant, not the idea of immaturity.
senses.whyCN: 把心爱的人叫作 baby，借的是照料婴儿时的那份温柔，而不是「幼稚」的意思。

intro.en: Baby is a word built to sound small.
intro.cn: baby 是一个听起来就小的词。

items.en: babe meant 'an infant'.
items.cn: babe 意为「婴儿」。

items.en: the ending -y made a pet form.
items.cn: 后缀 -y 构成昵称形式。

items.en: baby replaced babe in common use.
items.cn: baby 在日常使用中取代了 babe。

items.en: It extended to small things and loved ones.
items.cn: 它扩展到小东西与心爱的人。

items.en: Baby remains both a noun and an adjective.
items.cn: 如今仍兼作名词与形容词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ba opening; the near-meaning group gives words for the very young.
note.cn: 形近组都以 ba 开头；近义组是表示幼小孩子的词。

definition_en: the rear part of the body or thing, or to support someone
core_image: 一个人背对着门站着，肩胛骨绷紧
scene: 教室里有人从后面拍了他一下。He turned his back to the window.
sceneCN: 这里 back 是「背部」（第 1 个义项：身体后面的部分）；句意是他把背转向了窗户。

derivatives.zh: 由 back 加 -ward 构成，义为「向后的」
由 back 加 -ing 构成，义为「支持；后盾」
由 back 与 up 复合而成，义为「备份；后援」

senses.title: The rear of the body
senses.definition: the part of the body from the shoulders to the hips, opposite the chest
senses.definitionCN: 身体从肩到臀、与胸部相对的部分
senses.example: My back hurts after the long drive.
senses.exampleCN: 长途开车后我的背很疼。
senses.why: Back is an old Germanic word for the ridge of the body, and most later senses grow from that physical ridge.
senses.whyCN: back 是日耳曼语中表示身体脊背的老词，后来大多数义项都从这条「脊」长出来。

senses.title: The rear part
senses.definition: the part of something that is furthest from the front
senses.definitionCN: 某物离前面最远的部分
senses.example: Write your name on the back of the card.
senses.exampleCN: 把名字写在卡片的背面。
senses.why: If the back is the far side of a body, then the far side of any object is also its back.
senses.whyCN: 如果背部是身体的远侧，那么任何物体的远侧也能叫 back。

senses.title: Toward the rear or a former place
senses.definition: toward the rear, or to a place you came from
senses.definitionCN: 向后，或回到原来的地方
senses.example: She stepped back and let him pass.
senses.exampleCN: 她后退一步让他过去。
senses.why: Movement toward the back of a space, or back to an earlier place, produced the adverb use.
senses.whyCN: 朝空间的后方移动，或回到先前的地方，就产生了副词的用法。

senses.title: To support
senses.definition: to give help or approval to someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 给某人或某事帮助或认可
senses.example: The whole town backed the new school.
senses.exampleCN: 全镇都支持这所新学校。
senses.why: To back someone originally meant to stand at their back as support, and the physical position became the metaphor.
senses.whyCN: back 某人原指站在他背后撑腰，这个身体位置后来变成了比喻。

intro.en: Back is a word about the ridge of the body and everything behind it.
intro.cn: back 说的是身体的脊背，以及脊背后面的一切。

items.en: bæc meant 'the back'.
items.cn: bæc 意为「背部」。

items.en: bak kept the bodily sense.
items.cn: bak 保留身体义。

items.cn: back 扩展到物体的后部。

items.en: The adverb back meant 'to a former place'.
items.cn: 副词 back 意为「回原处」。

items.en: The verb back means to support.
items.cn: 动词 back 意为「支持」。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ack ending; the near-meaning group gives rear and support words.
note.cn: 形近组都以 ack 结尾；近义组是表示后部与支持的词。

definition_en: the area behind the main subject, or a person's past experience
core_image: 舞台后面一块素色幕布，演员站在幕布前
scene: 画家把最后一个人物放进画面。The mountains form a quiet background.
sceneCN: 这里 background 是「背景」（第 1 个义项：画面中主体后面的部分）；句意是群山构成了一片安静的背景。

derivatives.zh: 基础词，义为「后部」，background 由其与 ground 复合而成
由 background 加 -er 构成，义为「背景简报」

senses.title: The area behind
senses.definition: the area or scenery behind the main object
senses.definitionCN: 主体后面的区域或景物
senses.example: The mountains form a quiet background.
senses.exampleCN: 群山构成了一片安静的背景。
senses.why: Background is simply back plus ground, the ground at the back of a picture, so its first sense is spatial.
senses.whyCN: background 就是 back 加 ground，即画的后方那片地，所以第一个义项是空间性的。

senses.title: Past experience
senses.definition: the family, education and experience that shaped a person
senses.definitionCN: 塑造一个人的家庭、教育与经历
senses.example: Her background in science helped the team.
senses.exampleCN: 她的科学背景帮了团队。
senses.why: The ground behind a figure is not seen in detail but supports it, just as a person's past supports what they do now.
senses.whyCN: 人物背后的那片地看不真切，却托着人物，正如一个人的过去托着他现在做的事。

senses.title: Behind the main activity
senses.definition: the less visible part of a situation or activity
senses.definitionCN: 情况或活动中不太显眼的部分
senses.example: Several helpers worked in the background.
senses.exampleCN: 几位助手在幕后工作。
senses.why: If the background is what lies behind the subject, then people who work out of sight are working in the background.
senses.whyCN: 如果背景是主体后面的东西，那么看不见的人在做事，就是在幕后工作。

intro.en: Background is a compound of two plain English words.
intro.cn: background 是两个朴素的英语词复合而成。

items.cn: bæc 意为「背部」。

items.en: grund meant 'the ground'.

items.en: the compound named the ground behind a painted figure.
items.cn: 复合词指画中人物后面的地。

items.en: It extended to a person's past.
items.cn: 它扩展到指一个人的过去。

items.en: It also names the unseen part of activity.
items.cn: 如今也指活动中看不见的部分。

note.en: The look-alike group all end in ground; the near-meaning group gives setting and history words.
note.cn: 形近组都以 ground 结尾；近义组是表示环境与经历的词。

normal.en: Family background names where a person comes from.

abstract.en: See a row of helpers moving in the dim light.
abstract.cn: 想象一排助手在暗光里忙碌。

sensesIntro.en: The ground behind a figure, a person's past and unseen work are one spatial idea stretched in time.
sensesIntro.cn: 人物身后的地、个人的过去与看不见的工作，是同一个空间想法在时间上的延伸。

definition_en: toward the back, or in the opposite order
core_image: 一段录像被倒着播放，水往杯子里回去
scene: 视频播放器被人按了回放键。The film ran backwards for a few seconds.
sceneCN: 这里 backwards 是「倒着」（第 2 个义项：顺序相反地）；句意是影片倒着放了几秒钟。

derivatives.zh: 基础形容词，义为「向后的」，backwards 为其副词形式
由 backward 加 -ness 构成，义为「落后」

senses.title: Toward the back
senses.definition: in the direction of the back
senses.definitionCN: 朝背部的方向
senses.example: She stepped backwards without looking.
senses.exampleCN: 她没看就向后退了一步。
senses.why: Backwards is the adverb form of backward, and the -s ending marks an old genitive that became part of the word.
senses.whyCN: backwards 是 backward 的副词形式，词尾的 -s 原是古属格标记，后来固定进了单词。

senses.title: In reverse order
senses.definition: in the opposite order or direction
senses.definitionCN: 以相反的顺序或方向
senses.example: The film ran backwards for a few seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 影片倒着放了几秒钟。
senses.why: Moving backwards reverses space, and the same reversal applies to time and order, so counting and reading can also go backwards.
senses.whyCN: 向后移动反转了空间，同样的反转也适用于时间与顺序，所以数数和阅读也能倒着来。

senses.title: Making no progress
senses.definition: toward a worse or earlier state
senses.definitionCN: 朝更糟或更早的状态
senses.example: The business went backwards last year.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司去年倒退了。
senses.why: If forward is progress, moving backwards is losing ground, which gives the figurative sense of decline.
senses.whyCN: 如果说 forward 是进步，那么往后退就是失地，于是有了「退步」的比喻义。

intro.en: Backwards is an old direction word with a settled -s ending.
intro.cn: backwards 是一个词尾带 -s 的古老方向词。

items.en: bæc meant 'the back'.
items.cn: bæc 意为「背部」。

items.en: bakward meant 'toward the back'.
items.cn: bakward 意为「朝向后方」。

items.en: the -s form became a separate adverb.
items.cn: 带 -s 的形式成为独立副词。

items.en: backwards and backward both served as adverbs.
items.cn: backwards 与 backward 都曾作副词。

items.en: British English prefers backwards, American English backward.
items.cn: 英式英语多用 backwards，美式多用 backward。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -wards ending; the near-meaning group gives reverse and rearward words.
note.cn: 形近组都以 -wards 结尾；近义组是表示反向与后方的词。

normalIntro.en: Backwards can reverse a step, a count or a whole business.
normalIntro.cn: backwards 能让一步、一段数数或整桩生意反过来。

normal.en: British English uses backwards for the adverb more often than backward.
normal.cn: 英式英语副词更常用 backwards。

normal.en: Count backwards from ten is a common classroom task.
normal.cn: 从十倒着数是常见的课堂任务。

normal.en: Backwards and forwards means moving to and fro.
normal.cn: backwards and forwards 意为来回移动。

normal.en: The word always ends in -s.
normal.cn: 这个词总以 -s 结尾。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: BACK-wards.
normal.cn: 重音在第一音节。

abstract.en: See a film playing in reverse.
abstract.cn: 想象一段倒着播放的影片。

abstract.en: See a number line read from right to left.
abstract.cn: 想象一条从右往左读的数轴。

abstract.en: See a walker leaving heel prints first.
abstract.cn: 想象走路的人先留下脚跟印。

examples.en: The business went backwards last year.

sensesIntro.en: Going back, reversing order and losing ground are one movement read in space, time and value.
sensesIntro.cn: 向后退、把顺序倒过来与失去进展，是同一种移动在空间、时间与价值上的读法。

definition_en: meat from a pig that is salted or smoked
core_image: 平底锅里几片咸肉卷起油亮的边
scene: 清晨的厨房里油声滋滋作响。The bacon curled in the hot pan.
sceneCN: 这里 bacon 是「培根」（第 1 个义项：腌制或熏制的猪肉）；句意是培根在热锅里卷起了边。

derivatives.zh: 由 bacon 加 -er 构成，义为「适于制培根的猪」
由 bacon 加 -y 构成，口语中义为「有培根味的」

senses.title: Cured pork
senses.definition: meat from a pig that has been salted or smoked
senses.definitionCN: 经过盐腌或熏制的猪肉
senses.example: The bacon curled in the hot pan.
senses.exampleCN: 培根在热锅里卷起了边。
senses.why: Bacon comes from Old French bacon, which named the back and sides of a pig, so the meat word began as a cut of the animal.
senses.whyCN: bacon 来自古法语 bacon，原指猪的背部和两侧，所以这个肉名起初指的是一块部位。

senses.title: Money to live on
senses.definition: money earned to support a family, used in informal phrases
senses.definitionCN: 养家糊口的钱，用于口语说法
senses.example: He works two jobs to bring home the bacon.
senses.exampleCN: 他打两份工来养家。
senses.why: Because bacon was a valuable food, bringing it home became a picture of earning a living.
senses.whyCN: 因为培根曾是贵重食物，把培根带回家就成了挣钱养家的画面。

senses.title: Rescue from trouble
senses.definition: saved from a difficult situation, in the phrase save one's bacon
senses.definitionCN: 在 save one's bacon 这一说法中指使某人免遭殃
senses.example: The extra copy saved my bacon.
senses.exampleCN: 多出的那份副本救了我。
senses.why: If bacon is what keeps a household fed, saving it means saving what matters most, and the phrase widened to any rescue.
senses.whyCN: 如果培根是一家人吃饭的依靠，那么保住它就等于保住最要紧的东西，这个说法后来泛指任何解救。
